problem: VLN evaluation relies on endpoint success rate and path-alignment metrics on R2R/RxR, which hide which atomic instruction concepts models understand (random agents score non-trivially, models barely react to interventions), so VLN performance may be overestimated.
motivation: SOTA models appear close to human performance on R2R, yet simple instruction interventions (e.g. swapping left/right or the landmark) often leave predictions unchanged, and LMM-based agents do surprisingly poorly. A fine-grained diagnosis of atomic capabilities is needed to guide future language-guided navigation systems.
key_idea: Build a context-free grammar of VLN instructions (semi-automatically with GPT-4), derive five atomic instruction categories from it, and generate a diagnostic dataset (NavNuances) with category-specific path proposal and evaluation protocols.
insight: Gains on R2R are largely explained by vertical movement and region recognition, which dominate R2R instructions (over 35% involve stairs), while numerical comprehension stagnates near random-with-priors baselines (HAMT/ScaleVLN ≈ Agent 1*, far below Agent 2*). Supervised models show heavy left/right selective bias (Dual SR drops sharply; ScaleVLN 18.23% higher on right turns), whereas zero-shot LLM agents are nearly unbiased and better at landmark recognition, showing that large-model pretrained knowledge helps. Rule-based explicit directional actions help turning, and NavGPT4v's direct vision beats caption-based NavGPT4 on landmarks.
method: CFG construction: quadruple (N,T,P,S) at the concept level; GPT-4 parses R2R/RxR instructions and flags unparsable parts; about ten rounds of manual refinement until no omissions are found

Atomic categories: five categories induced from CFG rules: Direction Change (ActionT), Vertical Movement (ActionS), Numerical Comprehension, Landmark Recognition (ActionO+Landmark), Region Recognition (ActionR+Region)

Data generation pipeline: rule-based candidate path proposal on 90 Matterport3D scenes using Habitat semantic annotations, CFG-driven instruction templates, human refinement/annotation, and LLM rephrasing for linguistic diversity; GPT-4V is used to describe landmark instances
Paired/negative data: paired left/right turns from the same start view, paired up/down stairs, and numerical paths with same start but different ordinal/side used as negatives

Category-specific protocols: direction sector accuracy of the first sub-path (120° arcs); distance-based 3 m success for VM/LR/NU (NU also requires nDTW to be closer to GT than other paths in the set); inclusion-based success for region entering/exiting; Dual SR for left/right pairs
NavGPT4v baseline: NavGPT with actual panoramic images fed to GPT-4-vision plus modified prompt aligning photo indices to view directions

setting.backbone: Benchmark paper; evaluated Seq2Seq, CLIP-ViL, VLN-BERT, HAMT, DUET, BEVBERT, ScaleVLN (supervised) and NavGPT (GPT-3.5, GPT-4), NavGPT4v (GPT-4-vision, frozen, zero-shot)
setting.training_data: Supervised baselines fine-tuned on R2R (differing pretraining data, ScaleVLN uses large synthetic data); NavGPT4v is training-free
setting.observation: front-view RGB, panorama RGB, or text descriptions of panorama (captions), or panorama images for NavGPT4v
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoint selection (rule-based actions for Seq2Seq/CLIP-ViL)
setting.privileged: none (GT annotations used only for evaluation)

numbers.eval_set_note: NavGPT4v evaluated on a random subset of around 130 samples (to limit API cost); dataset has 579 DC / 170 VM / 78 NU / 275 RR / 685 LR instances
numbers.extra: R2R unseen numbers are reproduced results, also on subset

numbers.eval_set_note: NavGPT4v evaluated on random subset of about 130 samples
numbers.evidence: Table 1, R2R unseen columns, NavGPT4v row

numbers_note: Benchmark is the paper's own; 'test' split label is used for NavNuances as it has no official splits. Per-category numbers for baselines omitted per rules. Some results only in figures.
results: On NavNuances, zero-shot GPT-4-based agents beat supervised models on direction change (NavGPT4v 92.68 vs best supervised 79.62 HAMT) and landmark recognition (62.87 vs ≤36.78), but are much worse on vertical movement (13.64 vs ScaleVLN 84.71) and region recognition. All models remain far below humans (NU 89.13) on numerical comprehension, and supervised models show strong left/right selective bias.
limitations: Static discrete Matterport3D scenes cannot be edited, limiting diversity (no object-level counting, no attribute-level variation)
Only atomic instructions are evaluated, not long multi-step instructions or error correction
Small sizes for some categories (NU 78 instances) and zero-shot LLMs evaluated on only ~130 samples; CFG construction still needs manual correction
